name: University of Eastern Finland
summary: Two-campus university in Joensuu and Kuopio; eight English bachelor's, from data engineering and forestry to planetary health and East Slavic studies.

ib.text: Selection differs by programme: some keep a small certificate-based group for IB holders, others use an entrance exam course, interview or SAT. An IB in English, English A, or English B at 5 proves English.

programmes.name: Bachelor's and Master's Degree Programme in Data Engineering
programmes.about: Broad foundations plus specialised data technology, in a combined five-year bachelor's and master's, taught on either the Joensuu or the Kuopio campus.
programmes.overview: You study computer science, mathematics and engineering together with the legal, ethical and economic sides of data, with a focus on data technologies across the whole pipeline, from collecting and storing data to analysing it. Through freely chosen minor studies you can lean towards data storage, data analysis or machine learning. A bachelor's thesis and an internship are part of the degree, and the master's thesis is typically practical work done in a company. The three-year bachelor's flows directly into the two-year master's within the same programme, and it is taught on the Joensuu and Kuopio campuses.
programmes.ib: 10 of the 40 places per campus go to certificate-based (IB) applicants; the other 30 are chosen on SAT and a video.
programmes.selectionNote: Per campus: 30 places on SAT (1250+, maths 650+) plus a video; 10 on certificates such as the IB, 5 of them for spring-2027 graduates. No waiting list.

programmes.name: Bachelor's and Master's Degree Programme in Information Technology
programmes.about: A three-year IT bachelor's to European standards with direct continuation to a two-year master's, aiming for jobs in Finnish ICT companies; Joensuu or Kuopio.
programmes.overview: You study basic and advanced programming, algorithms, data management, software design and human-computer interaction, and add one or two minor subjects such as data science, business, law, social sciences or environmental sciences. Teaching is on campus in Joensuu and Kuopio, with some courses shared with a local university of applied sciences, and some companies offer internships and thesis placements. The university works actively with local IT companies, and the bachelor's flows directly into the master's within the programme. Graduates are aimed at careers in Finnish ICT companies, with research options and a doctoral programme open for those who want them.
programmes.ib: No IB route: selection is by an online entrance examination course and a video interview.
programmes.selectionNote: Per campus: 40 places by an online entrance exam course (by 14 Mar 2027) and a video interview; 10 via UEF Open University studies. IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Human and Planetary Health
programmes.about: Human biology, global and planetary health and evidence-based health promotion, taught in English in Kuopio with Finnish offered to help you settle in Finland.
programmes.overview: You study human biology and health (anatomy, physiology, pathology, microbiology, nutrition and pharmacology), global and planetary health (environmental health, public health, climate and health) and health promotion and disease prevention, linking the molecular, individual and population levels. Teaching uses lectures, seminars and laboratory work, with a bachelor's thesis, optional practical training and project work, and Finnish language studies throughout. Four university departments run the programme on the Kuopio campus. Graduates work in public health, health promotion and planetary health in NGOs, policy bodies and research, or continue to master's studies in toxicology or public health.
programmes.ib: 10 of 30 places on certificates such as the IB, 5 of them for spring-2027 graduates; 20 by SAT; no waiting list.
programmes.selectionNote: 20 places on SAT (1050+); 10 on certificates such as the IB, 5 of them for spring-2027 graduates. No waiting list.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in East Slavic Societies and Religion
programmes.credential: Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Theology
programmes.about: East Slavic languages (practical Russian and Ukrainian) combined with cultural expertise and theology, studying how religion shapes East Slavic societies.
programmes.overview: You choose one of two majors with shared foundations: East Slavic Languages and Cultures, leading to a Bachelor of Arts, or Orthodox Theology, leading to a Bachelor of Theology. The studies cover Russian and Ukrainian language, East Slavic cultural studies, Orthodox theology and the part religion plays in society, taking an interdisciplinary approach that joins humanities and theology and builds practical language skills and intercultural competence through work with original sources. Pathways suit both native speakers and learners of the languages. Graduates are prepared for work in education, public administration, international organisations, journalism and civil society.
programmes.selectionNote: A recorded online video interview (five questions, 25 points) decides; the top 10 are admitted and there is no waiting list. IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Lifelong Learning and Sustainable Development
programmes.about: Education studies with professional skills and theory, building towards international master's programmes, with room for a large minor.
programmes.overview: You study education and learning across the life course, looking at how learning supports social and cultural sustainability: education policy and systems, adult education, active citizenship and non-formal education, as well as statistical and qualitative research methods. Teaching includes project-based learning and service learning with working-life organisations, an internship and a bachelor's thesis with a preparatory seminar. The focus is on learning in associations, workplaces, organisations and civic movements rather than on classroom teacher training. Graduates can work in educational planning and policy, development projects and adult education, or continue to one of the university's international master's programmes.
programmes.ib: Has a certificate-based admission group for IB holders; results 31 May 2027.
programmes.selectionNote: 18 places by online interview (15–21 Feb 2027); 4 on certificates such as the IB (54+ points), 2 of them for spring-2027 graduates; 3 via open university. No waiting list.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Social Sciences
programmes.about: Sociology with social and public policy, focusing on key theories and research methods, taught mainly online with optional lectures on the Joensuu campus.
programmes.overview: You study sociology and social and public policy, with themes such as labour, education, care, multiculturalism and information technology, and ask how wellbeing, alienation and culture shape society and its policies. Courses are taught through lectures, seminars and reading groups, with assessment by learning journals, essays and exams, and you learn methods for collecting and analysing data on current social issues. A minor subject lets you widen the degree. Delivery is hybrid and does not require you to be on campus, which makes this the only bachelor's programme in social science in Finland taught in English.
programmes.ib: No IB route: 25 places by entrance exam and interview, up to 5 on previous studies.
programmes.selectionNote: 25 places by entrance examination and interview; up to 5 on previous university studies. IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Sustainable Forest Bioeconomy
programmes.about: Sustainable forest management, the bioeconomy and forest ecosystems, and their role in adapting to and mitigating climate change, in national and international settings.
programmes.overview: You study forest ecology, biodiversity and management, forest mensuration and remote sensing, forest technology, wood science, economics and policy, with a distinctive emphasis on information and communication technology for sustainable forest management. The first year covers fundamentals and methods, the second sustainable management, and the third regional development, networking and an exchange period, with field work, a professional internship and a bachelor's thesis. You choose a minor such as computer science, sustainable business or environmental policy. Graduates become foresters, forest data scientists, GIS analysts or policy experts, or continue to master's programmes in European or transatlantic forestry.
programmes.ib: Selection by an online entrance examination course, with maths and theory parts, and a video interview.
programmes.selectionNote: Online entrance exam course, theory and maths (9 Feb–2 Mar 2027), then up to 60 get a video interview (19–28 Mar). IB grades do not count; no waiting list.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Urban Sustainability Studies
programmes.about: A YUFE joint programme mixing social, natural and technical sciences and humanities to understand how cities and rural areas use natural resources and lead sustainable change.
programmes.overview: You study cities and sustainability across the social sciences, natural sciences, technical sciences and humanities, and build your own profile with three minors chosen from over 20 themes such as Urban Ecology, Sustainable Business, Smart Cities, Urban Health and Wellbeing and Post-growth Cities. The first year is at the home university, and the second and third are spent at two or more partner universities in Europe within a joint degree run by ten universities, with a mix of on-site and online courses and work on real sustainability challenges with students, teachers and businesses. The degree ends with a bachelor's thesis.
programmes.ib: Has a certificate-based selection group for IB holders.
programmes.selectionNote: 20 places by online interview (15–21 Feb 2027); 10 on certificates (54+ points). Studyinfo gives spring-2027 graduates 2 or 5 of those 10; its texts disagree.

notes: Joensuu and Kuopio are about 130 km apart; Data Engineering and IT are taught on both campuses, so you pick one when you apply.
In several programmes the IB counts for only a handful of places, and the rest go through an online entrance course, interview or SAT.
Several programmes keep no waiting list: if you are not admitted in the first round, you are rejected.
